content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target)**

The agreement imposes a classic multi-year take-or-pay on Tri City: a minimum monthly fee / Monthly Base Fee (§8.1(ii)) payable in advance for the full eight-year Term (§8.13, definition of "Term"), a mandatory obligation to source all bundled Services from M&I "during the Term" (§10.3.A), and an exit only on payment of a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value calculated off that minimum (§1.N, §11.1). No reduction right and no true-up exist anywhere, so all three fallback elements fail.

**Cure (shortest complete fallback change):**
1. New §8.1A — commitment limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period, reducible on thirty (30) days' notice, and any shortfall paid as a true-up with no penalty or shortfall charge.
2. Conforming edit to §10.3.A so the bundled-sourcing period tracks the same twelve-month period and expressly yields to the new reduction right (otherwise the retained "during the Term" sourcing mechanic would defeat the reduction).

Preferred (no minimum at all) was not pursued because deleting the Monthly Base Fee would require collateral rewrites to the payment, bundling and termination-fee machinery; the ERV-based termination fee itself is left to the T4C rule rather than double-flagged here.
